claims.feature: other: what Kay actually did on the Silmarillion
claims.claim: Kane says Christopher Tolkien gave remarkably little insight into the final step in which he created the published work with Kay's help.
claims.source: Douglas C. Kane, interviewed at TheOneRing.net about Arda Reconstructed, 2009
claims.quote: he created the final publish work with Guy Kay's help
claims.page: interview, 'how did this book come about' answer

claims.feature: other: what Kay actually did on the Silmarillion
claims.claim: Ordway reports that Kane's answer to whether the editorial cuts changed Tolkien's prose style for the worse seems to be yes.
claims.source: Holly Ordway, review of Arda Reconstructed, Mythprint / The Mythopoeic Society
claims.quote: Kane's answer seems to be yes

claims.feature: other: biography of the Silmarillion year
claims.claim: Rettino's thesis dates Kay's becoming an editor of The Silmarillion to 1974, citing Ordway.
claims.source: Matthew Rettino, 'Fantasies of History', 2012 McGill honours thesis, hosted at brightweavings.com
claims.quote: he became an editor of The Silmarillion in 1974

claims.feature: other: Tolkien as influence after the Silmarillion year
claims.claim: Ordway says the strongest single literary influence on Kay's Fionavar Tapestry is Tolkien, a natural result of his co-editing The Silmarillion.
claims.source: Holly Ordway, 'The World-Building of Guy Gavriel Kay' (1998 independent study, UMass Amherst), hosted at brightweavings.com
claims.quote: The strongest single literary influence on Kay's creation of The Fionavar

claims.claim: Rettino reports that in his introduction to Beyond this Dark House the poet Don Coles writes that Kay has an ease with crafting words in prose or poetry.
claims.source: Matthew Rettino, review of Beyond this Dark House, matthewrettino.com, 7 February 2014
claims.quote: Coles writes that Kay has an ease with crafting words

claims.claim: Rettino notes that one poem in Beyond this Dark House is dedicated to J.R.R. Tolkien.
claims.source: Matthew Rettino, review of Beyond this Dark House, matthewrettino.com, 7 February 2014
claims.quote: nods towards his relationship with J. R. R. Tolkien

claims.claim: Macpherson says Dunnett's every researched detail is seamlessly woven in, offering a sensory experience of sounds, tastes, colours and textures.
claims.source: Marie Macpherson, The Writers' Writer, Dorothy Dunnett Centenary (Dorothy Dunnett Society)
claims.quote: every detail is seamlessly woven into her astonishing tapestries

claims.feature: other: Kay and the Dunnett Society
claims.claim: Kay was the keynote speaker at the Dorothy Dunnett Centenary Gathering in 2023.
claims.source: The Writers' Writer, Dorothy Dunnett Centenary (Dorothy Dunnett Society)
claims.quote: author and keynote speaker @ DD Centenary Gathering 2023

claims.feature: other: Kay and Dunnett in person
claims.claim: Kay says Dunnett was wonderful in person and not only in print, across many encounters.
claims.source: Guy Gavriel Kay, The Writers' Writer, Dorothy Dunnett Centenary (Dorothy Dunnett Society)
claims.quote: she was wonderful in person, not just in print

claims.feature: other: biography of the Silmarillion year
claims.claim: Kay says he met Dorothy Dunnett in spring 1975 while living in a village outside Oxford working on the papers that became The Silmarillion.
claims.source: Guy Gavriel Kay, 'In Memoriam - Dorothy Dunnett', Locus Magazine, December 2001, reproduced at brightweavings.com
claims.quote: working on the papers that became The Silmarillion

claims.feature: other: what Kay actually did on the Silmarillion
claims.claim: Kay says going through the Tolkien correspondence was a part of the editing process he worked on.
claims.source: Guy Gavriel Kay, 'In Memoriam - Dorothy Dunnett', Locus Magazine, December 2001, reproduced at brightweavings.com
claims.quote: which was a part of the editing process

claims.feature: other: silence about the editing method
claims.claim: Kay says he did not discuss the details of editing The Silmarillion with Dunnett in 1975 and still does not.
claims.source: Guy Gavriel Kay, 'In Memoriam - Dorothy Dunnett', Locus Magazine, December 2001, reproduced at brightweavings.com
claims.quote: I didn't discuss the details of editing The Silmarillion

claims.claim: Spangenberg says the quantity of literary allusions and quotations in the Lymond Chronicles drew her into a paper chase after Dunnett's sources.
claims.source: Lisa L. Spangenberg, 'The Books of Dorothy Dunnett', Digital Medievalist / Celtic Studies Resources
claims.quote: enticed me into a paper chase as I tried to locate

claims.claim: Spangenberg says the two Dunnett Companion books supply the sources and even the translations for many of the allusions in the novels.
claims.source: Lisa L. Spangenberg, 'The Books of Dorothy Dunnett', Digital Medievalist / Celtic Studies Resources
claims.quote: offer the sources and even the translations, for many of the allusions

claims.quote: had to look up the former
